Treat agentic systems as bounded loops over plans, state, tools, observations, and stopping conditions. Prefer deterministic workflows when they meet the need more reliably.

items.title: Creating tool interfaces
items.text: Creating tool interfaces describes one part of a controlled action loop. The model may propose a step, but the application should independently validate the arguments, check the caller's permissions, enforce step/time limits, and record the actual tool result before deciding what happens next.

items.title: Interpreting tool-call requests
items.text: Interpreting tool-call requests belongs to the application integration boundary. Validate inputs before sending them, keep credentials on the server, handle non-success responses and cancellation, and log request metadata without storing secrets or unnecessary personal content. Provider-specific payloads must be checked against the selected API's current documentation.

content.task: Practice defining a narrow task within building a simple agent: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.
